closure_notes: La Factoría confirmed open as of 2025 — still ranked on World's 50 Best Bars list.
Lote 23 confirmed open; underwent minor vendor refresh in 2024 but core food hall intact.
La Respuesta (Santurce) confirmed open as of late 2025 — La Junta Wednesday salsa nights ongoing.
Noise Kitchen — verify before visiting; this Condado bar went through a rebrand in late 2024. Listed here under original concept; confirm hours on Instagram.
Bacardí Casa Cataño tour (formerly Casa Bacardí Visitor Center) rebranded/expanded in 2024 — 'La Rumba del Ron' experience added.
El Batey (Old San Juan dive bar) confirmed still operating despite recurring 'closing' rumors.
Caribbean Cinemas (Metro, Fine Arts) both confirmed open.

items.name: La Factoría
items.hours: Mon–Thu 6 PM–3 AM, Fri–Sat 6 PM–4 AM, Sun 6 PM–2 AM
items.description: Puerto Rico's most decorated bar, ranked in the World's 50 Best Bars list, with six interconnected rooms each pouring a different cocktail program — from tropical agave sours to barrel-aged rum old fashioneds.
items.why_it_matters: The only bar in Puerto Rico ever ranked in the World's 50 Best Bars; this is the cocktail world's equivalent of a Michelin star in San Juan.
items.walkability_from_old_san_juan: Walking distance — 205 Calle San Sebastián, heart of Old San Juan

items.name: La Placita de Santurce (Nightlife Circuit)
items.hours: Thu–Sat from ~8 PM; peak 10 PM–2 AM
items.description: By day, Santurce's municipal produce market; by night, Puerto Rico's best street-party nightlife scene — a dozen bars spill into an open plaza, live salsa and reggaeton compete, cold Medalla flows, and locals vastly outnumber tourists.
items.why_it_matters: This is where San Juan actually parties — no velvet rope, no cover charge, just an open-air block of bars that merge into one giant street celebration on weekends.
items.walkability_from_old_san_juan: 15-min Uber/taxi or 20-min walk across Dos Hermanos bridge into Santurce
items.dress_code: Casual — locals dress up, but jeans and a nice top is fine

items.name: El Batey
items.description: A gloriously grungy Old San Juan institution: dollar bills stapled to the ceiling, walls covered in graffiti, a jukebox loaded with classic rock and salsa, and the cheapest rum-and-Cokes in the city.
items.why_it_matters: Every bartender in San Juan has a El Batey story — it's a rite of passage and the great equalizer between tourists, expats, and born-and-raised locals.
items.walkability_from_old_san_juan: Walking distance — 101 Calle del Cristo, Old San Juan

items.name: Lote 23
items.type: Food hall and outdoor bar village
items.hours: Wed–Thu 5 PM–12 AM, Fri 5 PM–1 AM, Sat 12 PM–1 AM, Sun 12 PM–10 PM
items.description: An Instagram-worthy converted parking lot turned 20-vendor food hall in Santurce, with craft beer, rum cocktails, live DJs on weekends, and a rotating lineup of Puerto Rico's most creative food stalls — all under string lights and open sky.
items.why_it_matters: Lote 23 is the best single-stop answer to 'where can I drink well AND eat well in one place?' — especially perfect if your group can't agree on a restaurant.
items.walkability_from_old_san_juan: 15-min Uber; not easily walkable from Old San Juan

items.name: Pirilo Rooftop at AC Hotel Condado
items.hours: Daily 5 PM–12 AM (kitchen closes at 10 PM)
items.description: San Juan's most accessible rooftop bar with unobstructed Atlantic Ocean views, a curated rum cocktail menu, and shareable pizzas — the sunset hour here is legitimately one of the best in the Caribbean.
items.why_it_matters: Rooftop bars in Condado with actual ocean views are rarer than they look — this one delivers the view without the velvet-rope attitude of the casino hotel bars nearby.
items.walkability_from_old_san_juan: 20-min Uber from Old San Juan; walkable within Condado
items.dress_code: Smart casual — no flip-flops after 7 PM

items.name: La Junta Salsa Night at La Respuesta
items.hours: Wednesdays ~9 PM–2 AM; venue opens earlier for dinner
items.description: Every Wednesday, La Respuesta in Santurce hosts La Junta — one of San Juan's most authentic salsa social nights. DJs spin classic salsa, mambo, and Afro-Caribbean rhythms; the floor fills with serious dancers and welcoming beginners.
items.why_it_matters: This is what real San Juan salsa culture looks like — not a tourist show, but a neighborhood gathering that has been running every Wednesday for years.
items.dress_code: Casual but move-friendly — locals wear going-out clothes that allow dancing

items.name: Salsa Dancing at Nuyorican Café
items.type: Live salsa music venue and dance floor
items.hours: Fri–Sat 9 PM–3 AM; occasional Thursdays — check Facebook for schedule
items.description: The Nuyorican Café is Old San Juan's premier live salsa venue: a small, packed room where local bands play hard bop salsa and bomba, and the dance floor erupts from the first song. Friday nights are the crown jewel.
items.why_it_matters: With live bands rather than DJs, this is the closest thing to a 1970s Fania Records session you'll find in modern San Juan — intimate, loud, and absolutely electric.
items.walkability_from_old_san_juan: Walking distance — 312 Calle San Francisco, Old San Juan
items.dress_code: Smart casual — people dress up to dance here

items.name: Grupo Folclórico Afroboriqueño — Bomba & Plena Workshop
items.type: Cultural dance and percussion workshop (bomba & plena)
items.hours: Saturdays 2 PM–4 PM (recurring); private bookings available
items.description: A 2-hour participatory workshop in Puerto Rico's two indigenous Afro-Caribbean musical forms — bomba (drum-driven call-and-response dance) and plena (sung street music). Taught by working folklórico musicians, not resort entertainers.
items.why_it_matters: Bomba is to Puerto Rico what flamenco is to Spain — learning it from real practitioners, not a hotel activity desk, is the difference between a souvenir and a memory.
items.walkability_from_old_san_juan: 15-min Uber to Santurce community arts centers
items.dress_code: Comfortable clothes you can move in

items.name: Bacardí Casa Cataño — La Rumba del Ron Distillery Experience
items.hours: Mon–Sat 9 AM–4:30 PM, Sun 10 AM–4:30 PM (last tour 2 hours before close)
items.description: The world's largest premium rum distillery offers guided tours of the Casa Bacardí grounds with three tastings including limited-reserve expressions. The 'La Rumba del Ron' upgrade adds cocktail making and behind-the-barrels access.
items.why_it_matters: Bacardí produces 20 million cases of rum per year on this island — understanding its production at the source, a 10-minute ferry ride from Old San Juan, is an experience no rum lover should skip.
items.walkability_from_old_san_juan: 10-min ATA ferry from Pier 2 in Old San Juan to Cataño; distillery is a short taxi from the dock
items.dress_code: Casual — closed-toe shoes recommended for distillery floor

items.name: Old San Juan Rum & Mofongo Food Walking Tour
items.hours: Departures Fri–Sun at 11 AM and 2 PM; 2.5–3 hours
items.description: A guided walk through Old San Juan's colonial streets that pairs Puerto Rico's two greatest contributions to the world — rum cocktails and mofongo — with stops at 5–6 local bars and fondas (family restaurants) in the historic district.
items.why_it_matters: Cuts through tourist-trap menus to take you inside the spots locals actually eat, with a guide who can explain the African, Spanish, and Taino roots behind each dish.
items.walkability_from_old_san_juan: Starts in Old San Juan — no transportation needed
items.dress_code: Comfortable walking shoes — cobblestones are uneven

items.name: Spiga Cocina Criolla — Puerto Rican Cooking Class
items.hours: Sat–Sun 10 AM–1 PM; private evening sessions available on request
items.description: A hands-on 3-hour cooking class taught by a Puerto Rican chef in a fully equipped kitchen: you'll make sofrito from scratch, learn the achitote-fat technique behind authentic rice, prep pernil, and finish with a guided rum pairing of the meal you just cooked.
items.why_it_matters: You leave able to actually recreate Puerto Rican food at home — the sofrito lesson alone is worth the price of admission.

items.name: Flavors of San Juan — Santurce Street Food and Bar Tour
items.description: An evening tour of Santurce's art district and La Placita area: 4–5 stops covering pincho stands, craft beer at local taprooms, a piragua (shaved ice) tradition break, and at least one cocktail bar with a local bartender introduction.
items.why_it_matters: Santurce is the city's creative capital and its food scene is evolving faster than most guidebooks can track — a local guide is the fastest way to stay current.

items.name: Instituto de Cultura Puertorriqueña — Bomba en la Terraza
items.type: Outdoor cultural performance (free bomba & plena concerts)
items.hours: Saturdays ~5 PM–8 PM (check ICP calendar — not every weekend)
items.description: The Instituto de Cultura Puertorriqueña hosts free outdoor bomba and plena performances on its terrace inside Casa del Libro and surrounding Old San Juan plazas — rotating community ensembles, occasional nationally known musicians, and open-air dancing on cobblestones.
items.why_it_matters: The rare cultural experience that is genuinely free, genuinely local, and genuinely not designed for tourists — stumbling into one of these sets is a trip highlight.
items.walkability_from_old_san_juan: Walking distance — 500 Blvd del Valle, Old San Juan

items.name: Caribbean Cinemas Fine Arts — Cine de Arte & Cultural Screenings
items.hours: Daily; matinees from 12 PM, evening shows through 10 PM
items.description: The Fine Arts location of Caribbean Cinemas in Miramar/Santurce is Puerto Rico's only dedicated art-house theater, screening international films, Puerto Rican indie productions, and Oscar foreign-film contenders — many with Spanish subtitles and occasional director Q&As.
items.why_it_matters: A rainy afternoon or a quiet night here drops you into the Puerto Rican cultural conversation that hotel lobbies and beach clubs never show you.
items.walkability_from_old_san_juan: 15-min Uber to Fine Arts Miramar; not walkable

items.name: Don Q Rum at Serrallés — La Ruta del Ron Tasting Experience (Ponce + OSJ)
items.type: Premium rum tasting (curated rum flight + pairing)
items.hours: Thu–Sun 4 PM–8 PM at partnered Old San Juan locations; full Ponce distillery tour by appointment
items.description: Puerto Rico's #1 locally-owned rum (Serrallés family, since 1865) presented as a guided 5-rum flight covering agricole, cristal, aged, and limited expressions — either in Old San Juan pop-up format or as a day trip to the Ponce distillery castle.
items.why_it_matters: Don Q outsells Bacardí in Puerto Rico 3:1 yet gets almost no tourist attention — tasting it properly, with context, corrects the most common gap in visitors' rum education.
items.walkability_from_old_san_juan: Old San Juan tasting: walking distance. Ponce distillery: 90-min drive south — best as a dedicated day trip.
